o: Kassim era un hombre enfermizo, joyero de profesión, bien que no tuviera tienda establecida.
t: Kassim was a sickly man, a jeweler by trade, though he had no established shop.

o: Trabajaba para las grandes casas, siendo su especialidad el montaje de las piedras preciosas.
t: He worked for the great houses, his specialty being the setting of precious stones.

o: Pocas manos como las suyas para los engarces delicados.
t: Few hands like his for delicate mountings.

o: Con más arranque y habilidad comercial, hubiera sido rico.
t: With more initiative and commercial savvy, he would have been rich.

o: Pero a los treinta y cinco años proseguía en su pieza, aderezada en taller bajo la ventana.
t: But at thirty-five he was still going about his business in his room, fitted out as a workshop beneath the window.

o: Kassim, de cuerpo mezquino, rostro exangüe sombreado por rala barba negra, tenía una mujer hermosa y fuertemente apasionada.
t: Kassim, of meager build, with a bloodless face shadowed by a sparse black beard, had a beautiful woman, fiercely passionate.

o: La joven, de origen callejero, había aspirado con su hermosura a un más alto enlace.
t: The young woman, of street origins, had aspired with her beauty to a higher match.

o: Esperó hasta los veinte años, provocando a los hombres y a sus vecinas con su cuerpo.
t: She waited until she was twenty, teasing men and her neighbors with her body.

o: Temerosa al fin, aceptó nerviosamente a Kassim.
t: Fearful in the end, she nervously accepted Kassim.

o: No más sueños de lujo, sin embargo.
t: No more dreams of luxury, however.

o: Su marido, hábil--artista aún,--carecía completamente de carácter para hacer una fortuna.
t: Her husband, a skillful—still an artist—man, was wholly lacking in the character to make a fortune.

o: Por lo cual, mientras el joyero trabajaba doblado sobre sus pinzas, ella, de codos, sostenía sobre su marido una lenta y pesada mirada, para arrancarse luego bruscamente y seguir con la vista tras los vidrios al transeunte de posición que podía haber sido su marido.
t: So while the jeweler worked bent over his pliers, she, elbows propped, held on her husband a slow, heavy gaze, then tore herself away and followed with her eyes, through the glass, the passerby whose station in life might have been her husband's.

o: Cuanto ganaba Kassim, no obstante, era para ella.
t: Whatever Kassim earned, nonetheless, was hers.

o: Los domingos trabajaba también a fin de poderle ofrecer un suplemento.
t: On Sundays he worked too, so as to be able to give her a little extra.

o: Cuando María deseaba una joya--¡y con cuánta pasión deseaba ella!--trabajaba de noche.
t: When María wanted a piece of jewelry—and with what passion she wanted it!—he worked at night.

o: Después había tos y puntadas al costado; pero María tenía sus chispas de brillante.
t: Afterward there came coughing and stitches in his side; but María had her flashes of brilliance.

o: Poco a poco el trato diario con las gemas llegó a hacerle amar las tareas del artífice, y seguía con ardor las íntimas delicadezas del engarce.
t: Little by little, the daily handling of gems came to make her love the craftsman's tasks, and she followed ardently the intimate subtleties of the setting.

o: Pero cuando la joya estaba concluída--debía partir, no era para ella,--caía más hondamente en la decepción de su matrimonio.
t: But when the jewel was finished—and it had to be, it was not for her—she fell more deeply into the disappointment of her marriage.

o: Se probaba la alhaja, deteniéndose ante el espejo.
t: She tried on the ornament, pausing before the mirror.

o: Al fin la dejaba por ahí, y se iba a su cuarto.
t: At last she left it lying there and went off to her room.

o: Kassim se levantaba al oir sus sollozos, y la hallaba en la cama, sin querer escucharlo.
t: Kassim would get up on hearing her sobs, and find her in bed, not wanting to hear it.

o: --Hago, sin embargo, cuanto puedo por ti,--decía él al fin, tristemente.
t: "I do, however, all I can for you," he would say at last, sadly.

o: Los sollozos subían con esto, y el joyero se reinstalaba lentamente en su banco.
t: The sobs welled up with this, and the jeweler slowly took his place again on his bench.

o: Estas cosas se repitieron, tanto que Kassim no se levantaba ya a consolarla.
t: These things repeated themselves, so that Kassim no longer got up to comfort her.

o: ¿de qué? Lo cual no obstaba para que Kassim prolongara más sus veladas a fin de un mayor suplemento.
t: of what? Which did not prevent Kassim from prolonging his evening vigils in order to earn a greater supplement.

o: Era un hombre indeciso, irresoluto y callado.
t: He was an indecisive, irresolute, silent man.

o: Las miradas de su mujer se detenían ahora con más pesada fijeza sobre aquella muda tranquilidad.
t: His wife's glances now lingered with heavier fixity upon that mute tranquility.

o: --¡Y eres un hombre, tú!--murmuraba.
t: "And you are a man, you!" he murmured.

o: Kassim, sobre sus engarces, no cesaba de mover los dedos.
t: Kassim, over his settings, never ceased to move his fingers.

o: --No eres feliz conmigo, María--expresaba al rato.
t: "You are not happy with me, María," he would say after a while.

o: --¡Feliz! ¡Y tienes el valor de decirlo!
t: "Happy! And you have the nerve to say it!"

o: ¿Quién puede ser feliz contigo?
t: Who can be happy with you?

o: ¡Ni la última de las mujeres!...
t: Not the last of women!...

o: ¡Pobre diablo!--concluía con risa nerviosa, yéndose.
t: "Poor devil!" he would conclude with a nervous laugh, as he went away.

o: Kassim trabajaba esa noche hasta las tres de la mañana, y su mujer tenía luego nuevas chispas que ella consideraba un instante con los labios apretados.
t: Kassim worked that night until three in the morning, and his wife then had new sparks, which she considered for a moment with pursed lips.

o: --Sí... ¡no es una diadema sorprendente!...
t: "Yes... it is not a surprising diadem!..."

o: ¿cuando la hiciste?
t: When did you make it?

o: --Desde el martes--mirábala él con descolorida ternura--dormías de noche...
t: "Since Tuesday"—he looked at her with pale tenderness—"you slept at night..."

o: --¡Oh, podías haberte acostado!...
t: "Oh, you could have gone to bed!..."

o: ¡Inmensos, los brillantes!
t: Huge, the shining ones!

o: Porque su pasión eran las voluminosas piedras que Kassim montaba.
t: Because her passion was the voluminous stones that Kassim set.

o: Seguía el trabajo con loca hambre de que concluyera de una vez, y apenas aderezada la alhaja, corría con ella al espejo.
t: She followed the work with a mad hunger for it to be finished at last, and as soon as the jewel was ready, she ran with it to the mirror.

o: Luego, un ataque de sollozos.
t: Then, a fit of sobbing.

o: --¡Todos, cualquier marido, el último, haría un sacrificio para halagar a su mujer!
t: "Everyone, any husband, the last man alive, would make a sacrifice to please his wife!"

o: Y tú... y tú... ni un miserable vestido que ponerme, tengo!
t: And you... and you... I haven't even a miserable dress to put on!

o: Cuando se franquea cierto límite de respeto al varón, la mujer puede llegar a decir a su marido cosas increíbles.
t: When a certain limit of respect for the man is crossed, the woman may end up saying incredible things to her husband.

o: La mujer de Kassim franqueó ese límite con una pasión igual por lo menos a la que sentía por los brillantes.
t: Kassim's wife crossed that limit with a passion at least equal to the one she felt for the diamonds.

o: Una tarde, al guardar sus joyas, Kassim notó la falta de un prendedor--cinco mil pesos en dos solitarios.--Buscó en sus cajones de nuevo.
t: One afternoon, putting away her jewels, Kassim noticed the brooch was missing--five thousand pesos in two solitaires.--He searched his drawers again.

o: --¿No has visto el prendedor, María? Lo dejé aquí.
t: "Haven't you seen the brooch, María? I left it here."

o: --¿Dónde está?--se volvió extrañado.
t: "Where is it?"--he turned, puzzled.

o: Su mujer, los ojos encendidos y la boca burlona, se erguía con el prendedor puesto.
t: His wife, eyes blazing and mouth mocking, stood with the brooch on.

o: --Te queda muy bien--dijo Kassim al rato.--Guardémoslo.
t: "It suits you very well," Kassim said after a while.--"Let's keep it."

o: ¡Cómo te duele pensar que podría ser mío...
t: How it hurts to think it could be mine...

o: Mañana te lo doy.
t: Tomorrow I'll give it to you.

o: Hoy voy al teatro con él.
t: Today I'm going to the theater with him.

o: --Haces mal... podrían verte.
t: "You're doing wrong... they might see you."

o: Perderían toda confianza en mí.
t: They'd lose all confidence in me.

o: --¡Oh!--cerró ella con rabioso fastidio, golpeando violentamente la puerta.
t: "Oh!"--she closed the door with furious annoyance, slamming it violently.

o: Vuelta del teatro, colocó la joya sobre el velador.
t: On her return from the theater, she placed the jewel on the nightstand.

o: Kassim se levantó y la guardó en su taller bajo llave.
t: Kassim got up and locked it away in his workshop.

o: Al volver, su mujer estaba sentada en la cama.
t: When he came back, his wife was sitting on the bed.

o: --¡Es decir, que temes que te la robe!
t: "So you're afraid I'll steal it from you!"

o: ¡Qué soy una ladrona!
t: "What am I, a thief!"

o: Has sido imprudente, nada más.
t: You were just careless, that's all.

o: --¡Ah! ¡Y a ti te lo confían!
t: "Ah! And they trust you with it!"

o: ¡Y cuando tu mujer te pide un poco de halago, y quiere... me llamas ladrona a mí! ¡Infame!
t: And when your wife asks you for a little flattery, and wants... you call me a thief! Infamous!

o: Se durmió al fin.
t: She finally fell asleep.

o: Pero Kassim no durmió.
t: But Kassim did not sleep.

o: Entregaron luego a Kassim para montar, un solitario, el brillante más admirable que hubiera pasado por sus manos.
t: They then handed Kassim the solitaire to mount, a solitaire, the most brilliant one that had ever passed through his hands.

o: --Mira, María, qué piedra.
t: "Look, María, what a stone."

o: No he visto otra igual.
t: I've never seen another like it.

o: Su mujer no dijo nada; pero Kassim la sintió respirar hondamente sobre el solitario.
t: His wife said nothing; but Kassim felt her breathing deeply over the solitaire.

o: --Una agua admirable...--prosiguió él--costará nueve o diez mil pesos.
t: "A marvelous water..." he went on, "it will cost nine or ten thousand pesos."

o: --Un anillo!--murmuró María al fin.
t: "A ring!" María murmured at last.

o: --No, es de hombre... Un alfiler.
t: "No, it's a man's... A pin."

o: A compás del montaje del solitario, Kassim recibió sobre su espalda trabajadora cuanto ardía de rencor y cocotaje frustrado en su mujer.
t: In time with the mounting of the solitaire, Kassim received on his hard-working back all that burned with resentment and frustrated coquetry in his wife.

o: Diez veces por día interrumpía a su marido para ir con el brillante ante el espejo.
t: Ten times a day she interrupted her husband to go with the brilliant stone to the mirror.

o: Después se lo probaba con diferentes vestidos.
t: Then she tried it on with different dresses.

o: --Si quieres hacerlo después...--se atrevió Kassim.--Es un trabajo urgente.
t: "If you want to do it later..." Kassim ventured. "It's an urgent job."

o: Esperó respuesta en vano; su mujer abría el balcón.
t: He waited for an answer in vain; his wife was opening the balcony door.

o: --María, te pueden ver!
t: --María, they can see you!

o: --Toma! ¡ahí está tu piedra!
t: --Here! There's your stone!

o: El solitario, violentamente arrancado, rodó por el piso.
t: The solitaire, violently torn away, rolled across the floor.

o: Kassim, lívido, lo recogió examinándolo, y alzó luego desde el suelo la mirada a su mujer.
t: Kassim, livid, picked it up and examined it, then raised his gaze from the floor to his wife.

o: --Y bueno, ¿por qué me miras así?
t: --Well, why are you looking at me like that?

o: ¿Se hizo algo tu piedra?
t: Has something happened to your stone?

o: Y reanudó en seguida su tarea, aunque las manos le temblaban hasta dar lástima.
t: And he immediately resumed his task, though his hands trembled pitifully.

o: Pero tuvo que levantarse al fin a ver a su mujer en el dormitorio, en plena crisis de nervios.
t: But in the end he had to get up to see his wife in the bedroom, in the midst of a full nervous crisis.

o: El pelo se había soltado y los ojos le salían de las órbitas.
t: Her hair had come loose and her eyes bulged from their sockets.

o: --¡Dame el brillante!--clamó.--¡Dámelo!
t: --Give me the brilliant!--she cried.--Give it to me!

o: ¡Nos escaparemos!
t: We'll get away!

o: ¡Para mí! ¡Dámelo!
t: To me! Give it to me!

o: --María...--tartamudeó Kassim, tratando de desasirse.
t: --María...--Kassim stammered, trying to pull free.

o: --¡Ah!--rugió su mujer enloquecida.--¡Tú eres el ladrón, miserable!
t: --Ah!--his wife raged, beside herself.--You're the thief, you wretch!

o: ¡Me has robado mi vida, ladrón, ladrón!
t: You've stolen my life, thief, thief!

o: Y creías que no me iba a desquitar... cornudo!
t: And you thought I wouldn't get even with you... you bastard!

o: ¡Ajá! Mírame... no se te había ocurrido nunca, ¿eh?
t: Ah! Look at me... it had never occurred to you, had it?

o: ¡Ah!--y se llevó las dos manos a la garganta ahogada.
t: --Ah!--and she clamped both hands to her choking throat.

o: Pero cuando Kassim se iba, saltó de la cama y cayó, alcanzando a cogerlo de un botín.
t: But as Kassim was leaving, she sprang from the bed and fell, managing to catch hold of him by the boot.

o: ¡El brillante, dámelo!
t: The shiny one — give it to me!

o: ¡No quiero más que eso!
t: I want nothing else!

o: ¡Es mío, Kassim miserable!
t: It's mine, you miserable Kassim!

o: Kassim la ayudó a levantarse, lívido.
t: Kassim helped her to get up, livid.

o: Después hablaremos... acuéstate.
t: We'll talk about it later... go to bed.

o: --Bueno, veremos si es posible... acuéstate.
t: "Well, we'll see if it's possible... go to bed.

o: La bola montó de nuevo a la garganta.
t: The ball rose again in her throat.

o: Kassim volvió a trabajar en su solitario.
t: Kassim went back to work in his solitude.

o: Como sus manos tenían una seguridad matemática, faltaban pocas horas ya.
t: Since his hands had a mathematical sureness, it was already nearly time.

o: María se levantó para comer, y Kassim tuvo la solicitud de siempre con ella.
t: María got up to eat, and Kassim made his usual request of her.

o: Al final de la cena su mujer lo miró de frente.
t: At the end of dinner his wife looked him straight in the face.

o: --Es mentira, Kassim--le dijo.
t: "It's a lie, Kassim," she said.

o: --¡Oh!--repuso Kassim sonriendo--no es nada.
t: "Oh!" Kassim replied, smiling. "It's nothing."

o: --¡Te juro que es mentira!--insistió ella.
t: "I swear it's a lie!" she insisted.

o: Kassim sonrió de nuevo, tocándole con torpe cariño la mano.
t: Kassim smiled again, touching her hand with clumsy affection.

o: --¡Loca! Te digo que no me acuerdo de nada.
t: "You're crazy! I'm telling you I don't remember anything.

o: Y se levantó a proseguir su tarea.
t: And he got up to go on with his task.

o: Su mujer, con la cara entre las manos, lo siguió con la vista.
t: His wife, her face in her hands, followed him with her eyes.

o: --Y no me dice más que eso...--murmuró.
t: "And all he says to me is that..." she murmured.

o: Y con una honda náusea por aquello pegajoso, fofo e inerte que era su marido, se fue a su cuarto.
t: And with a sudden nausea at that sticky, soggy, inert thing her husband was, she went off to her room.

o: No durmió bien.
t: She didn't sleep well.

o: Despertó, tarde ya, y vio luz en el taller; su marido continuaba trabajando.
t: She woke up, late already, and saw light in the workshop; her husband was still working.

o: Una hora después, éste oyó un alarido.
t: An hour later, he heard a scream.

o: --Sí, es para ti; falta poco, María--repuso presuroso, levantándose.
t: "Yes, it's for you; it won't be long, María," he replied hastily, rising to his feet.

o: Pero su mujer, tras ese grito de pesadilla, dormía de nuevo.
t: But his wife, after that nightmare cry, had fallen asleep again.

o: A las dos de la mañana Kassim pudo dar por terminada su tarea; el brillante resplandecía, firme y varonil en su engarce.
t: At two in the morning Kassim was able to consider his task finished; the brilliant shone, firm and manly in its setting.

o: Con paso silencioso fue al dormitorio y encendió la veladora.
t: He went silently to the bedroom and lit the bedside lamp.

o: María dormía de espaldas, en la blancura helada de su camisón y de la sábana.
t: María was sleeping on her back, in the icy whiteness of her nightgown and the sheet.

o: Fue al taller y volvió de nuevo.
t: He went to the workshop and came back again.

o: Contempló un rato el seno casi descubierto, y con una descolorida sonrisa apartó un poco más el camisón desprendido.
t: He gazed a while at the nearly bared breast, and with a faded smile drew the slipping nightgown a little further aside.

o: Su mujer no lo sintió.
t: His wife did not feel it.

o: No había mucha luz.
t: There wasn't much light.

o: El rostro de Kassim adquirió de pronto una dura inmovilidad, y suspendiendo un instante la joya a flor del seno desnudo, hundió, firme y perpendicular como un clavo, el alfiler entero en el corazón de su mujer.
t: Kassim's face suddenly took on a hard immobility, and, suspending the jewel for an instant against the bare breast, he drove the pin straight and perpendicular like a nail, all the way into his wife's heart.

o: Hubo una brusca apertura de ojos, seguida de una lenta caída de párpados.
t: There was a sudden opening of the eyes, followed by a slow falling of the lids.

o: Los dedos se arqueron, y nada más.
t: The fingers arched, and nothing more.

o: La joya, sacudida por la convulsión del ganglio herido, tembló un instante desequilibrada.
t: The jewel, shaken by the convulsion of the wounded ganglion, trembled for an instant, out of balance.

o: Kassim esperó un momento; y cuando el solitario quedó por fin perfectamente inmóvil, pudo entonces retirarse, cerrando tras de sí la puerta sin hacer ruido.
t: Kassim waited a moment; and when the solitary figure was at last perfectly still, he could then withdraw, closing the door behind him without a sound.
